title: Generation Capacity and Utilization Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/01 - Generation Capacity and Utilization Analysis.md
goal: To assess the operational efficiency and effectiveness of electricity generation assets by evaluating their capacity and utilization rates.
dataRequired: Installed generation capacity (MW) for each power plant.
Actual power generated over a specific period (Mffh).
Plant availability and downtime data (scheduled and unscheduled).
Seasonal or hourly demand data (optional for deeper insights).
Industry benchmarks for capacity utilization.
improve: Conduct a root cause analysis for plants with low capacity factors (e.g., maintenance issues, fuel supply constraints).
Optimize maintenance schedules to minimize downtime during peak demand periods.
Explore upgrades or retrofitting opportunities for underperforming plants to enhance efficiency.
Improve demand forecasting and load balancing to align generation with actual consumption.
Assess the feasibility of decommissioning chronically underutilized assets or replacing them with more flexible generation technologies.

formulas.source: Capacity Factor (%) = (Actual Power Generated (Mffh) / (Installed Capacity (MW) x Hours in Period)) x 100

title: Power Plant Performance and Efficiency Evaluation
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/02 - Power Plant Performance and Efficiency Evaluation.md
goal: To evaluate the overall performance and efficiency of power plants by examining key operational metrics such as thermal efficiency, output reliability, and energy conversion effectiveness.
dataRequired: Fuel input data (e.g., fuel type, quantity, and calorific value).
Electricity output data (e.g., net power generated in Mffh).
Heat rate data (if available).
Operational hours and downtime records.
Emission data (optional for advanced efficiency evaluations).
Industry benchmarks for similar power plant types.
improve: Implement regular maintenance schedules to enhance reliability and minimize forced outages.
Upgrade older equipment or adopt advanced technologies to improve thermal efficiency and reduce heat rate.
Optimize fuel procurement strategies to ensure consistent fuel quality.
Use predictive analytics and real-time monitoring systems to proactively identify and address inefficiencies.
Conduct employee training programs to improve operational best practices and reduce performance variability.

formulas.source: Thermal Efficiency (%) = (Net Electricity Output (Mffh) x 3.6) / (Fuel Input in GJ) x 100
Heat Rate (kJ/kffh) = Fuel Input (GJ) / Net Electricity Output (Mffh)

title: Heat Rate Degradation and Monitoring Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/03 - Heat Rate Degradation and Monitoring Analysis.md
goal: To assess and monitor changes in the heat rate of power plants over time, identify factors contributing to degradation, and propose strategies to maintain or improve efficiency.
dataRequired: Historical heat rate data (kJ/kffh or BTU/kffh) for the power plant.
Fuel input data (quantity and calorific value).
Net electricity output (Mffh).
Maintenance and downtime records.
Ambient conditions data (e.g., temperature, humidity).
Plant age and operational history.
Industry benchmarks for heat rate by generation type and age.
improve: Perform regular cleaning and maintenance of boilers, turbines, and heat exchangers to reduce fouling and improve efficiency.
Invest in advanced monitoring systems for real-time tracking of heat rate and operational anomalies.
Optimize operational practices, such as maintaining optimal load levels to avoid stress on equipment.
Upgrade aging equipment with energy-efficient alternatives to reduce heat rate degradation.
Implement predictive maintenance strategies to address potential issues before they affect performance.
Conduct periodic audits to ensure alignment with industry best practices and benchmarks.

formulas.source: Heat Rate (kJ/kffh) = Fuel Input (GJ) / Net Electricity Output (Mffh).

title: Capacity Factor and Forced Outage Rate Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/04 - Capacity Factor and Forced Outage Rate Analysis.md
goal: To evaluate the efficiency and reliability of power plants by analyzing their capacity factor and forced outage rate.
dataRequired: Installed capacity of each power plant (MW).
Actual electricity generated over a specified period (Mffh).
Total hours in the analysis period (e.g., year, month).
Total unplanned outage hours for each plant.
Industry benchmarks for capacity factors and forced outage rates by plant type.
improve: Perform root cause analysis for plants with high forced outage rates to identify and address recurring issues.
Implement predictive maintenance programs to prevent unplanned outages.
Optimize plant scheduling to improve alignment with demand and increase capacity factor.
Upgrade aging or underperforming equipment to reduce forced outages and enhance reliability.
Train operations staff to detect early signs of equipment failure and improve response times during outages.
Use real-time monitoring and data analytics to track performance and proactively address inefficiencies.

formulas.source: Capacity Factor (%) = (Actual Electricity Generated (Mffh) / (Installed Capacity (MW) x Total Hours in Period)) x 100
Forced Outage Rate (%) = (Forced Outage Hours / Total Hours in Period)

title: Peaking Plant Profitability and Dispatch Optimization
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/05 - Peaking Plant Profitability and Dispatch Optimization.md
goal: To evaluate the financial performance and operational efficiency of peaking power plants and optimize their dispatch strategies to maximize profitability while meeting peak demand requirements.
dataRequired: Electricity market prices (hourly or interval-based).
Variable operating costs (fuel, maintenance, startup costs).

Historical dispatch data (generation output during peak demand periods).
Peak demand patterns (seasonal and hourly).

improve: Implement advanced dispatch optimization tools that use real-time market data and predictive analytics to schedule generation during high-price periods.
Reduce variable operating costs through efficiency upgrades or renegotiation of fuel contracts.

Collaborate with grid operators to anticipate peak demand patterns and secure favorable pricing opportunities.

Conduct regular profitability reviews and adjust dispatch strategies based on evolving market conditions and cost structures.

formulas.source: Total Costs ($) = (Fuel Costs + Variable O&M Costs + Startup Costs) x Dispatched Hours
Net Profit ($) = Total Revenue - Total Operating Costs - Fixed Operating

formulas.source: Total Start-up Cost ($) = Fuel Cost + Labor Cost + Maintenance Cost
Total Shutdown Cost ($) = Residual Fuel Loss + Labor Cost + Preparation

formulas.source: REC Coverage (%) = (RECs Procured / Total Electricity Generated) x 100
Offset Coverage (%) = (Carbon Offsets Procured / Total GHG Emissions)

title: Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) Comparison
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/electricity-generation/12 - Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) Comparison.md
goal: To calculate and compare the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) for different generation technologies or plants.
dataRequired: Capital expenditure (CapEx) for each generation type or plant.
Fixed and variable operational expenditure (OpEx).
Fuel costs by generation type (if applicable).
Annual electricity generation (Mffh).
Plant lifespan and annual operating hours.
Discount rate (used to calculate present value).
Decommissioning costs (if applicable).
improve: Invest in efficiency upgrades to reduce OpEx and fuel costs, lowering overall LCOE.

formulas.source: Total Lifecycle Costs = CapEx + (Annual OpEx x Plant Lifespan) + Decommissioning Costs
Total Generation (Mffh) = Annual Electricity Generation (Mffh) x Plant
LCOE ($/Mffh) = Total Lifecycle Costs / Total Generation (Mffh)
Discounted LCOE = (Sum of Discounted Costs) / (Sum of Discounted Electricity Generation)

formulas.source: Spot Market Exposure (%) = (Spot Market Sales / Total Sales) x 100
Hedging Coverage (%) = (Hedged Volume / Total Generation Volume) x 100
